name: bonk-sir-g3-sunrise
notes: Sir Bonk ground.3 (anim.bonk.g3), 2026-10-22: Sunrise, the owner's 'upward slice meant to catch airbourne target', from the normals board (tmp/bonk-normals) and the Seedance 2.5 reference the owner approved (artifacts/video-refs/sir-bonk-normals/g3-sunrise), without its crouch (owner: 'the crouch for g3 is not necessary'). Two-handed like the video (the board had a free arm); no 'if you wait' wobble (normals stay simple). Today's move-data clock (125 ticks, plank hitbox 21-40, IASA 44). Replaces Reverse Rising Slash. Lessons from Barn Door built in: loose two-handed hold with elbows down (elbows='hands' overhead), carry both ways, flow in the first take, straight to idle after the return. Owner rule: show the keys, then the first take, before any revision.
character: Sir Bonk (68 joints: a Humanoid body with Mixamo names and full fingers; a 3x4 cape chain Cape_L/C/R1..4 under Spine2 that a spring drives in the game, so leave it at rest; a 2.26 m wooden plank greatsword fixed to the right hand as joint Weapon0, bladeHilt where its 1.42 m blade leaves the crossguard and bladeEnd at the tip)
description:
Sir Bonk's ground 3, Sunrise: his anti-air normal, one rising two-handed slash that scoops the plank up off the floor in front of him and up over his head, to catch someone jumping in at him. It replaces his old Reverse Rising Slash (reference 'rising' is not in this pack: there is no style reference; the video sets the poses).

Who he is. Sir Bonk is a huge, good-hearted, slightly dumb brute who read Don Quixote once and knighted himself (images 1 and 2). He has a blue mop-bucket helm with a broom crest, a cream tabard with his painted crown, pot-lid pauldrons and a cape, and he carries a plank greatsword. He is proud and determined. The owner wants his normals clean: no gags, the energy comes from his body.

His idle, where this move starts and ends (measured in the character frame, metres from the entry hips): feet wide and square to the front (foot joints about -0.89 up, the floor at -1.025). The plank rests back over his right shoulder: the right hand in front of the right chest (about 0.46 m above the hips), the blade rising behind him to his right, its tip about 1.15 m behind his hips and 0.9 m above the hilt. The left fist sits on his left hip. His shoulders are about 0.53 m above the hips and his head joint 0.66 m; each arm reaches about 0.70 m from shoulder to wrist.

How the game plays it. Ticks 0-125 at 60 Hz, played once; the game stretches the whole clip over the move, so author exactly these ticks. The game crossfades into the clip from his idle or his run over 0.05 s. The plank itself is the hitbox (a 0.65 m capsule along it) from tick 21 to tick 40: from tick 21 it sweeps up through the space in front of him, and until tick 40 it covers the space above him that an opponent jumps in through. From tick 44 the player can act again: the scoop, the stretch and the return to the shoulder must all read by tick 44. Tick 0 is his idle pose exactly, and ticks 50-125 are his idle pose exactly (`b.exit_pose`); the game blends into the idle anyway, and the owner does not care about the part after the return.

The reference (image 3: nine frames of the video the owner approved, seen from his front three-quarter right, the camera of `front-three-quarter-right`; each frame's tick is in the brief's review beats). It sets the poses and the body mechanics, not the timing: the video takes about 4.5 s and holds every pose. Its dark flying blob and orange smears are video artifacts. The owner dropped the video's deep crouch (frames 3 and 4 squat to the floor): here he only dips.

The beats:
- Ticks 0-3: he leaves the idle. Its plank hand is folded back about 137 degrees off the forearm (hidden behind the plank); straighten that wrist by tick 4. The check skips ticks 0-3 for it.
- Ticks 3-7, the grip (video beat 2): the left hand leaves his hip and closes on the handle just below the right hand; the plank comes upright in front of his right shoulder and the knees start to give.
- Ticks 7-13, the drop (video beat 3, without its squat): a small dip, the hips 5-8 cm down, his eyes up and forward where an opponent jumps in. The plank swings down and back past his right leg, tip trailing behind him.
- Ticks 13-17, low (video beat 4, without its squat): the plank low by his right side, its tip a hand's width off the floor ahead of his right foot, both hands low by the right hip, the weight loaded into the legs. This is the squash.
- Ticks 17-21, rising (video beat 5): the legs drive him up and the plank scoops up through the space in front of him. At tick 21 (contact) it points forward and up, about 45 degrees, in front of his chest.
- Ticks 21-26, up (video beat 6): the plank passes vertical in front of him, his body stretching up behind it, the heels lifting. Fast.
- Ticks 26-30, sky (video beat 7): the stretch. Tall on his toes (both heels up), both hands overhead, the plank straight up at the sky, chest lifted and head up, hips 2-6 cm above the idle. A clean silhouette from the match camera.
- Ticks 30-38: a moving hold up there (the plank covers above him until tick 40): the stretch eases, the plank drifts a little back, the heels settle. Nothing parks.
- Ticks 38-40, down (video beat 8): the plank vertical in front of his face, heels down.
- Ticks 40-44, shoulder (video beat 9): the plank tips back onto his right shoulder and the left fist returns to his hip. By tick 44 he stands in his hero stance.
- Ticks 44-50: straight into his idle pose, no separate settle. The plank wrist bends back into the idle's fold over ticks 41-50 (the check skips ticks 41-125 for it). Ticks 50-125 hold the idle pose exactly.

Both hands, loosely. Both hands hold the handle from tick 5 to tick 40 (the brief's `two_hands`, held loosely: `two_hands_hold`). The left fist only has to sit on the handle beside the right hand, free to turn about it and slide along it: `two_hand_grip(..., hold='loose', elbows=True)` for the keys with the hands below the shoulders (grip, drop, low, rising), and `elbows='hands'` for the keys with the hands at or above the head (up, sky, the hold, down), where the elbows belong above the shoulders but still under the hands. Between the keys use `carry(clip, keys, hold='loose', elbows=..., both_ways=True)` (guide, Contacts), one call per stretch with the same elbows option as its keys (for example ticks 5-21 with elbows=True and 21-40 with 'hands'). The elbows never wing up and out sideways: Barn Door's first keys did, and the owner saw it at once.

The body drives the swing. The scoop comes from the legs: the dip loads them, and from tick 17 the knees and hips extend while the chest lifts, so the plank rises with his whole body and not his arms alone; the stretch at tick 30 is the release of the dip.

Flow from the first take. Barn Door's first take came out pose to pose (5.1 stops per joint per second) and needed a separate smoothing pass; this one should land in the hand-made range in one go. Follow the guide's Flow section: stagger the arrivals (the hips lead, the chest a tick or two later, the arms and head trail; a body part may meet its key up to 2 ticks early or late, the plank keeps its key ticks), make every hold a moving hold, let the spine flex against the hips and the head lag. Before saving, check the `flow:` metrics: under 1.0 stops per joint per second and under 30% of the body stopping together.

Both feet stay planted: the toes do not slide and the heels may lift. The plank stays clear of his bucket, crest, pauldrons, cape and legs, and its tip never goes into the floor (the floor is at up = -1.025 m in the character frame). The fighter does not move; the hips may shift. Do not animate the cape joints (Cape_L/C/R1..4): a spring drives them in the game, so leave them at their rest rotation. No props other than the plank. Keep each hand in line with its forearm (wrists under 45 degrees) outside the exempt ticks.
